narrator.name: Narrator
narrator.note: Reads all narration, speech introductions and glosses on names.

jacob.name: Jacob
jacob.note: The patriarch returning from Mesopotamia; aggrieved with Laban, fearful and deferential before Esau, commanding with his household.

sichem.name: Sichem
sichem.note: Son of Hemor, prince of the land; infatuated and eager.

hemor.name: Hemor
hemor.note: The Hevite ruler, father of Sichem; a persuasive negotiator.

hemor-and-sichem.name: Hemor and Sichem
hemor-and-sichem.note: Father and son persuading their townsmen at the city gate.

sons-of-jacob.name: The sons of Jacob
sons-of-jacob.note: Dina's brothers; coldly deceitful in the bargain, defiant after the slaughter.

1.t: And Dina the daughter of Lia went out to see the women of that country.

2.t: And when Sichem the son of Hemor the Hevite, the prince of that land, saw her, he was in love with her: and took her away, and lay with her, ravishing the virgin.

3.t: And his soul was fast knit unto her; and whereas she was sad, he comforted her with sweet words.

4.t: And going to Hemor his father, he said:
Get me this damsel to wife.

5.t: But when Jacob had heard this, his sons being absent, and employed in feeding the cattle, he held his peace till they came back.

6.t: And when Hemor the father of Sichem was come out to speak to Jacob,

7.t: Behold his sons came from the field: and hearing what had passed, they were exceeding angry, because he had done a foul thing in Israel, and committed an unlawful act, in ravishing Jacob's daughter.

8.t: The soul of my son Sichem has a longing for your daughter: give her him to wife:

9.t: And let us contract marriages one with another: give us your daughters, and take you our daughters.

10.t: And dwell with us: the land is at your command, till, trade, and possess it.

11.t: Sichem also said to her father and to her brethren:
Let me find favour in your sight, and whatsoever you shall appoint I will give:

12.t: Raise the dowry, and ask gifts, and I will gladly give what you shall demand: only give me this damsel to wife.

13.t: The sons of Jacob answered Sichem and his father deceitfully, being enraged at the deflowering of their sister:

14.t: We cannot do what you demand, nor give our sister to one that is uncircumcised; which with us is unlawful and abominable.

15.t: But in this we may be allied with you, if you will be like us, and all the male sex among you be circumcised:

16.t: Then will we mutually give and take your daughters, and ours; and we will dwell with you, and will be one people:

17.t: But if you will not be circumcised, we will take our daughter and depart.

18.t: Their offer pleased Hemor, and Sichem, his son:

19.t: And the young man made no delay, but forthwith fulfilled what was required: for he loved the damsel exceedingly, and he was the greatest man in all his father's house.

20.t: And going into the gate of the city, they spoke to the people:

21.t: These men are peaceable, and are willing to dwell with us: let them trade in the land, and till it, which being large and wide wanteth men to till it: we shall take their daughters for wives, and we will give them ours.

22.t: One thing there is for which so great a good is deferred: We must circumcise every male among us, following the manner of the nation.

23.t: And their substance, and cattle, and all that they possess, shall be ours; only in this let us condescend, and by dwelling together, we shall make one people.

24.t: And they all agreed, and circumcised all the males.

25.t: And behold the third day, when the pain of the wound was greatest: two of the sons of Jacob, Simeon and Levi, the brothers of Dina, taking their swords, entered boldly into the city and slew all the men.

26.t: And they killed also Hemor and Sichem, and took away their sister Dina out of Sichem's house.

27.t: And when they were gone out, the other sons of Jacob came upon the slain; and plundered the city in revenge of the rape.

28.t: And they took their sheep, and their herds, and their asses, wasting all they had in their houses and in their fields.

29.t: And their children and wives they took captive.

30.t: And when they had boldly perpetrated these things, Jacob said to Simeon and Levi:

You have troubled me, and made me hateful to the Chanaanites and Pherezites, the inhabitants of this land. We are few: they will gather themselves together and kill me; and both I, and my house shall be destroyed.

31.t: Should they abuse our sister as a strumpet?
31.q: Only Simeon and Levi answer; kept on the brothers' group voice rather than a separate pair.
